chunks: My father — may Allah be pleased with him — said in his letter to me:

Know, my son, that the best of the supererogatory prayers are the two rak'ahs of Fajr, then after them the one rak'ah of Witr, then after it the two rak'ahs of Zawal, then after them the supererogatory prayers of Maghrib, then after it the completion of the Night Prayer, and after it the completion of the daytime supererogatory prayers.

key_terms.رَكْعَةُ ٱلْوِتْرِ: the single rak'ah of Witr from the Night Prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا ٱلزَّوَالِ: the two rak'ahs performed at zawal
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا ٱلْفَجْرِ: the two units of prayer associated with Fajr as a highly emphasized voluntary prayer
key_terms.نَوَافِلُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ: the voluntary prayers performed after Maghrib

ai.seo_question: Which voluntary prayers are considered the best in this hadith from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This narration presents a ranking of the most excellent voluntary prayers, beginning with the two rak'ahs of Fajr and proceeding through Witr, Zawal, the nawafil of Maghrib, the rest of the Night Prayer, and then the daytime nawafil. It reflects the importance of regular supererogatory worship and the structured emphasis placed on certain prayers within devotional practice.
